title: Respiration Summary
content:
# Respiration Summary

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Summarise the key concepts of respiration
- Compare aerobic and anaerobic respiration
- Link respiration to other body systems
- Review key equations, terms, and experimental methods

## Introduction

This lesson brings together all the key concepts of respiration. Respiration is central to biology - it's how all living cells release energy from glucose. Understanding respiration helps explain exercise, metabolism, and how organisms survive in different conditions.

## Key Concepts

### Why Respiration Matters

**Central to life:**
- All living cells respire
- Provides energy for ALL life processes
- Links to nutrition, transport, and excretion
- Occurs continuously (24/7)

### The Big Picture

**Energy flow:**
$$\text{Sun} \xrightarrow{\text{photosynthesis}} \text{Glucose} \xrightarrow{\text{respiration}} \text{ATP} \xrightarrow{} \text{Cellular work}$$

### Key Equations Summary

**Aerobic respiration:**
$$C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2 \rightarrow 6CO_2 + 6H_2O + \text{energy}$$
(~36-38 ATP)

**Anaerobic respiration (animals):**
$$C_6H_{12}O_6 \rightarrow 2C_3H_6O_3 + \text{energy}$$
(~2 ATP, produces lactic acid)

**Anaerobic respiration (yeast/plants):**
$$C_6H_{12}O_6 \rightarrow 2C_2H_5OH + 2CO_2 + \text{energy}$$
(~2 ATP, produces ethanol + CO₂)

### Comparing Aerobic and Anaerobic

| Feature | Aerobic | Anaerobic |
|---------|---------|----------|
| Oxygen | Required | Not required |
| Location | Mitochondria | Cytoplasm |
| Products | CO₂ + H₂O | Lactic acid or ethanol + CO₂ |
| ATP yield | ~36-38 | ~2 |
| Efficiency | High | Low |
| Sustainability | Long-term | Short-term |

### ATP - The Energy Currency

**Key points:**
- Universal energy carrier
- Made during respiration
- Used for all cellular processes
- Rapidly recycled (~500 times/day)

**ATP cycle:**
$$\text{ADP} + P_i + \text{energy} \rightleftharpoons \text{ATP}$$

### Mitochondria Summary

| Structure | Function |
|-----------|----------|
| Outer membrane | Boundary |
| Inner membrane | Electron transport chain, ATP synthase |
| Cristae | Increase surface area |
| Matrix | Krebs cycle enzymes |
| DNA | Codes for some proteins |

### Respiratory Substrates Summary

| Substrate | Energy (kJ/g) | RQ | When used |
|-----------|---------------|-----|----------|
| Carbohydrates | ~16 | 1.0 | Normal activity |
| Lipids | ~39 | ~0.7 | Prolonged activity |
| Proteins | ~17 | ~0.9 | Starvation only |

### Exercise and Respiration Summary

| During exercise | After exercise |
|-----------------|----------------|
| ↑ Heart rate | Recovery time |
| ↑ Breathing rate | Oxygen debt repaid |
| ↑ Blood to muscles | Lactic acid removed |
| Anaerobic if intense | Stores restored |

### Oxygen Debt Summary

**Components:**
- Fast: Restore PC and O₂ stores (2-3 min)
- Slow: Remove lactic acid (up to 1 hour)

**Lactic acid fate:**
- ~65% oxidised
- ~20% → glucose (Cori cycle)
- ~10% → glycogen
- ~5% → protein

### Key Experiments Summary

| Experiment | What it shows |
|------------|---------------|
| Respirometer | O₂ consumption rate |
| Limewater | CO₂ production |
| Hydrogencarbonate indicator | CO₂ level changes |
| Heat production | Energy release |
| Fermentation tube | CO₂ from yeast |

### Links to Other Topics

| Topic | Connection to respiration |
|-------|---------------------------|
| Nutrition | Provides glucose |
| Transport | Delivers O₂, removes CO₂ |
| Excretion | CO₂ and water as waste |
| Photosynthesis | Opposite equation |
| Enzymes | Control respiration rate |
| Exercise | Increases respiration rate |
| Homeostasis | Maintains glucose levels |

### Common Calculations

**Cardiac output:**
$$\text{Cardiac output} = \text{Heart rate} \times \text{Stroke volume}$$

**Ventilation rate:**
$$\text{Ventilation rate} = \text{Breathing rate} \times \text{Tidal volume}$$

**Respiratory quotient:**
$$RQ = \frac{CO_2 \text{ produced}}{O_2 \text{ consumed}}$$

**Respiration rate:**
$$\text{Rate} = \frac{\text{Volume of O}_2 \text{ (or distance)}}{\text{Time}}$$

### Key Diagrams to Know

| Diagram | What to label |
|---------|---------------|
| Mitochondrion | Outer membrane, inner membrane, cristae, matrix |
| Respirometer | Organism, soda lime, coloured liquid, capillary tube |
| ATP cycle | ATP, ADP, Pᵢ, energy in/out |
| Oxygen debt graph | Oxygen deficit, steady state, oxygen debt |

### Practical Applications

| Application | Respiration principle |
|-------------|-----------------------|
| Brewing | Yeast fermentation → ethanol |
| Bread making | Yeast → CO₂ makes dough rise |
| Sports training | Improving aerobic capacity |
| Medicine | Understanding metabolic diseases |
| Food storage | Slowing respiration preserves food |

## Common Exam Questions

- Write equations for aerobic/anaerobic respiration
- Compare aerobic and anaerobic respiration
- Explain why exercise increases respiration rate
- Describe how to investigate respiration experimentally
- Calculate RQ and interpret results

## Common Misconceptions Review

| Misconception | Reality |
|--------------|---------|
| Respiration = breathing | Respiration is cellular; breathing is ventilation |
| Plants don't respire | All living things respire |
| Only animals do anaerobic | Yeast and plants can too |
| Energy is created | Energy is transferred, not created |
| Lactic acid causes days of soreness | DOMS is from muscle damage |
| All lactic acid becomes glucose | Most is oxidised |

## Practice Questions

1. Write the word equation for aerobic respiration. (2 marks)

2. State two differences between aerobic and anaerobic respiration. (2 marks)

3. Explain why mitochondria are described as the 'powerhouse of the cell'. (3 marks)

4. A student measures oxygen consumption during exercise. The RQ changes from 0.85 at rest to 1.1 during intense exercise. Explain what this shows. (4 marks)

5. Describe how you would use a respirometer to compare respiration rates in germinating and non-germinating seeds. (4 marks)

6. Compare the effects of aerobic and anaerobic respiration on muscle performance during a 400m sprint. Include the role of oxygen debt in recovery. (6 marks)

## Key Terms Review

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Respiration | Chemical reactions releasing energy from glucose |
| Aerobic | With oxygen |
| Anaerobic | Without oxygen |
| ATP | Energy currency molecule |
| Mitochondria | Site of aerobic respiration |
| Fermentation | Anaerobic respiration in yeast |
| Lactic acid | Product of anaerobic respiration in animals |
| Oxygen debt | Extra O₂ needed after exercise |
| RQ | Respiratory quotient (CO₂/O₂) |
| EPOC | Excess post-exercise oxygen consumption |

## Summary

- Respiration releases energy from glucose in all living cells
- Aerobic: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + ATP (~36-38)
- Anaerobic: glucose → lactic acid OR ethanol + CO₂ + ATP (~2)
- ATP is the universal energy currency
- Mitochondria are the main site (aerobic); cytoplasm (anaerobic)
- Exercise increases respiration; intense exercise triggers anaerobic
- Oxygen debt = extra oxygen needed after exercise for recovery
- RQ indicates which substrate is being respired
- Respiration links to nutrition, transport, excretion, and homeostasis
